user_query: Why does node2vec’s inability to reuse samples explain its strong Macro-F1 gains over LINE on BlogCatalog?
llm_response: Because node2vec generates many more distinct random-walk contexts than LINE’s edge-sampling objective, it can expose the classifier to a much richer set of neighborhood patterns on BlogCatalog, where labels are highly overlapping and depend on higher-order proximity. LINE’s samples are effectively one-shot edge observations, so it cannot repeatedly reuse the same local structure to reinforce useful signals. node2vec’s walk-based sampling therefore acts like a stronger data-augmentation mechanism, which helps the downstream classifier separate classes better and yields a much larger Macro-F1 improvement on BlogCatalog.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This explanation matches the standard intuition for node2vec versus LINE on overlapping-label social networks, but the exact causal wording depends on the specific experimental setup and paper interpretation.
